text:
sarah: FYI new upstream advisory - CVE-2026-3152 affecting OpenSSL 3.1.x and libcrypto. NVD link: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-3152. Observed in our ubuntu-jammy:base and in the alpine:3.18 images we build. CVSS 7.8 — exploitability looks remote but data exfil possible in certain TLS handshakes. recommend urgent triage and rebuild window.

mike: thanks. where was this detected? scan output or vendor alert? any PoC?

sarah: vendor advisory + our image-scan (grype) flagged it on latest nightly for jammy and alpine. no public PoC yet but upstream backported patches to 3.1.2k.

priya: can we get a quick delta of which of our images include affected packages? I can run a targeted SBOM query. prioritization depends on surface (hosted API vs internal infra).

jason: multiarch build matrix concern: arm64 builders often compile different openssl flags. we should rebuild amd64+arm64 and run regression tests. will need ~2h extra per arch in CI unless we parallelize.

chen: developer-facing SDK containers also pull ubuntu-latest -> will need pinned base for reproducible builds. we should avoid forcing app-level bump until infra images are ready.

alex: release window? we prefer a midnight UTC deploy for low traffic, but if severity high we can do a daytime hotfix with canary. what's security rec?

sarah: security recommends patch-and-rebuild images, sign them, canary for 1% traffic for 2h, then 10%/50%/100% if no regressions. if tests fail, auto-rollback.

mike: can we do a patchbackport for jammy instead of full distro upgrade? that reduces surface. for alpine we'll update apk package to the patched version.

jason: agreed. implement patch backport where available. for alpine need to ensure musl vs glibc differences — this CVE affects OpenSSL, not musl, so alpine is still in-scope.

chen: please add these steps to the base-image CI job:
```
- bump OPENSSL_VERSION=3.1.2k
- rebuild with --no-cache
- run ./ci/image-smoke.sh --parallel 8
- publish to staging registry with tag: staging-cve2026-<arch>
```

deploy-bot: CI triggered: base-image-rebuild-staging for jammy/amd64 started (job id: 78421).

priya: test matrix: unit smoke, start container, run tls-handshake-fuzzer, run runtime-latency-suite, run integration against internal test endpoints. we should schedule the fuzzer for extended 1h run on canary.

alex: who signs the images? we need KMS key rotation plan. current key is in project-prod KMS; do we want to use a dedicated key for base images?

sarah: ops/infra should create a dedicated KMS key with least privilege for image signing. audit logs MUST be enabled and forwarded to splunk. RBAC: only release-managers + eng-security can sign.

jason: I'll open an infra ticket to provision a new Cloud KMS key and update cosign config. Also will add a short playbook for rolling signatures.

mike: any expected runtime regressions? OpenSSL minor bumps sometimes change default ciphers. please run our TLS compatibility matrix (TLS 1.2/1.3 + legacy ciphers).

chen: noted. also update transitive deps in our language runtimes (python wheel manylinux, node binaries) — we should run dependency-graph scan to catch apps bundling libssl.

priya: risk tier: hosted api endpoints that terminate TLS on our side = P1. internal infra images that do not terminate TLS = P2. prioritize accordingly.

alex: propose schedule: today - triage + patch PRs, tomorrow morning - build + staging canary, 24h soak, then progressive rollout. agree?

mike: +1 from runtime. i'll watch flames during canary.

jason: provisioning KMS key now. ticket: INFRA-1412.

deploy-bot: Build 78421 jammy/amd64 finished -> pushed staging-cve2026-amd64: success.

chen: starting fuzzer on canary image now. will post logs in this thread.

priya: added SBOM diffs to the incident doc: https://confluence.internal/redwood/cve-2026-3152 (notes + remediation checklist).

sarah: action items: 1) jason -> KMS + cosign config (INFRA-1412). 2) mike -> run TLS matrix + regression tests. 3) chen -> update SDK/container pins + run fuzzer. 4) priya -> prioritize hosted api images in staging. 5) alex -> schedule canary window and owner. everyone please ack.

mike: ack.

jason: ack.

chen: ack.

priya: ack.

alex: ack.

sarah: thanks all. will follow up with remediation PRs and the rollout status here. :)
